lead: Overland Park is a city of homeowners and basements in one of the country's hail belts. Hail, flash flooding along Indian Creek and sump pump failures drive most of its water damage.
risk: hail damage, creek flooding and basement water
why: Johnson County gets hit by large hail almost every spring. Stones crack shingles, split siding and break skylights, and the leaks often show up weeks later in the next rain. Many Overland Park homes have finished basements, especially the newer houses in the south part of the city. When a sump pump fails or loses power in a storm, water can cover the floor in minutes.

Indian Creek and Tomahawk Creek wind through the city, and both can rise fast in heavy rain. Low areas near the creeks and their trails flood in big storms. North Overland Park has older homes from the 1950s and 1960s, with aging drains and supply lines. In these older homes, foundation cracks and floor drain backups are common sources of basement water.

image_caption: Spring hail in Johnson County cracks Overland Park roofs and siding.
problems: Finished basements in south Overland Park
Low areas near Indian and Tomahawk creeks
1950s and 1960s homes in north Overland Park
tips: Get the roof checked after any hail, even with no leak yet.
Add a battery backup sump pump and test it each spring.
Add water backup coverage to your policy; it is usually extra.
Keep gutters clear and downspouts pointed away from the house.
areas: Calls come from Downtown Overland Park, Corporate Woods, Deer Creek, Stanley, Nall Hills and Blue Valley, plus Olathe, Leawood and Lenexa.

faq.q: Does my Overland Park policy cover a flooded basement?
faq.a: It depends on the cause. A burst pipe is usually covered. A failed sump pump or floor drain backup needs a water backup endorsement. Water from a rising creek or surface runoff needs flood insurance. Check which of these your policy has before storm season.
